reasoning: A hybrid approach combines autonomous reasoning to identify obvious shared features across instances with XAI tools to quantify feature importance and detect spurious patterns. This ensures both intuitive pattern recognition and rigorous attribution validation, especially critical for spotting spurious correlations that may not be apparent through inspection alone.

autonomous_tasks.query: Identify which features are common across all three misclassified instances (13590, 2021, 21096) by cross-checking their input values.
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: A list of features that appear in all three instances

autonomous_tasks.query: Evaluate whether any shared feature (e.g., marital-status=Married-civ-spouse) has a semantic or social interpretation that may be spurious (e.g., correlates with income due to data leakage or bias in dataset), despite not being directly related to income.
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: A justification for why a shared feature may be spurious or misleading in context

tool_selection.reasoning: SHAP provides consistent, interpretable feature importance across instances, allowing us to identify which features have high attribution despite lacking semantic relevance. LIME and Integrated Gradients offer local interpretability to verify model reliance on specific features. Sensitivity analysis confirms whether removing a feature significantly alters predictions, indicating spurious dependency. Combining these tools ensures robust detection of shared spurious features with high statistical and logical confidence.
